name: table-sort
pattern: Sorting requests from native table column headers, following the APG Sortable Table Example and synchronizing aria-sort without changing native roles
responsibility: Handles sorting operations on consumer-authored native table headers and provides aria-sort, data-state, and sort-request events. Does not reorder rows, generate appearance/content, or write roles.

authorMarkup.sortable: Add data-table-sort-target="sortable", a nonempty table-unique data-table-sort-column identifier, and scope="col" to each sortable <th>.
authorMarkup.button: Place exactly one native <button> inside each sortable <th>; it handles activation and keyboard interaction.
authorMarkup.rows: The consumer writes thead/tbody structure, tr, th, and td elements.
authorMarkup.content: The controller generates no elements or content. The consumer or server reorders rows.

semanticElements: The root must be an HTMLTableElement.
Every sortable target must be a <th>.
Each sortable target must contain exactly one native <button>.
data-table-sort-column must be nonempty and unique within the table.
Sortable targets must not have colspan.
contractValidation.columnRationale: Headers with colspan refer to multiple columns, making event detail ambiguous. Rowspan does not break column correspondence and is allowed. Non-sortable cell spans are unrestricted because the controller does not use row/column indexes.
contractValidation.invalidMarkup: Validate markup on connection. Invalid markup prevents ARIA writes, listener registration, and state outputs and warns once per connection. Do not throw.
contractValidation.warning: Warnings identify table-sort controller, the required native table root, and the violated conditions.

completion.warning: List completed attributes using "Added <attributes>. Include them in your markup." Warn once per connection using a flag separate from the enhancement-disabling warning.

column.description: The active column's data-table-sort-column; an empty string means no sorting.

direction.description: Sort direction, following ARIA 1.2 aria-sort values.

column.description: Current sort column. Assignment changes aria-sort and state outputs without custom events.

direction.description: Current sort direction. Assignment changes aria-sort and state outputs without custom events.

table-sort:beforesort.when: Before a sort request caused by trusted sortable-button activation
table-sort:beforesort.effect: On preventDefault(), leave aria-sort and state outputs unchanged and do not emit table-sort:sort.

table-sort:sort.when: After a sort request caused by trusted sortable-button activation
table-sort:sort.effect: The controller does not reorder rows. The consumer or server handles this event and reorders the DOM.

events.detailType: Export the detail type as TableSortSortDetail from src/index.ts. beforesort and sort share one type because their detail shape is identical.
events.programmatic: column assignment, direction assignment, initialization, and reconnection do not emit custom events.
events.sameSort: Do not emit beforesort/sort when activation changes neither column nor direction.
events.synthetic: Ignore clicks with isTrusted=false, changing neither state nor custom events. HTMLElement.click() is also untrusted.

consumerIntegration.stimulusActions: Listen for table-sort:sort and table-sort:beforesort on the root or an ancestor. The controller does not stop propagation.
consumerIntegration.cancelableHook: Cancel sorting with event.preventDefault() in a table-sort:beforesort listener.
consumerIntegration.programmatic: Other controllers may access column and direction through a Stimulus controller reference or outlets. Programmatic API changes emit no events.
consumerIntegration.nested: Use :self or event.target === event.currentTarget when listening outside nested table-sort roots.
consumerIntegration.sorting: The consumer reorders rows after table-sort:sort, either by changing DOM order or requesting and rendering server results.
consumerIntegration.grid: Use grid on the same table when two-dimensional cell navigation is required. The controllers are independent and do not reference each other.

behavior.sorting: Do not reorder rows in the controller. Comparison depends on consumer data types, so emit a request event only.
behavior.sortToggle: Sortable-button activation cycles none -> ascending -> descending -> none. The third state provides a way to restore the unsorted initial state.
behavior.sortSingleColumn: At most one column has an active sort direction, following ARIA 1.2 guidance. Consumers may build multi-key sorting from event history.
behavior.keyboard: Delegate keyboard interaction to the native button inside sortable. Do not register keydown. Making th itself focusable would require roving tabindex and move toward a grid design.

managedMarkup.role: Do not write roles on the root or cells; retain native table semantics.
managedMarkup.scope: Supply scope="col" only when absent on a sortable target. Without scope, th columnheader determination depends on cells in the same row (WHATWG HTML Auto state); explicit scope avoids that structural dependency.
managedMarkup.sort: Synchronize sortable aria-sort with sorting state; set aria-sort="none" on inactive sortable columns.
managedMarkup.stateOnly: Only sortable-target data-state is controller-managed state output.
managedMarkup.preservation: Preserve authored id, scope, and other attributes. The controller synchronizes aria-sort.

stateOutputs.ownership: Only sortable data-state is controller-owned. Do not use ARIA as a visual state output or aggregate per-column state into root data-state.

lifecycle: Register root click in connect() and remove it in disconnect().
Track sortable target additions/removals through Stimulus TargetConnected/TargetDisconnected.
Leave written aria-sort, scope, and data-state on disconnect().
Synchronize aria-sort and state outputs with current markup on reconnection without reapplying initial values.
Do not duplicate listeners or custom events when reconnecting the same instance

observations.item: aria-sort announcements on column headers in a native table
observations.impact: Native table roles and aria-sort state are fixed; the consumer remains responsible for the actual sort.

acceptanceCriteria: Required AAA criteria: 2.1.3 Keyboard (No Exception), with no pointer-only features; and 3.2.5 Change on Request, with controller focus movement limited to user actions or consumer JS calls, never timers.
Preserve native table semantics without writing roles.
Only one column may have an active aria-sort direction.
Only trusted sortable activation emits one cancelable beforesort followed by one committed sort, in that order.
The controller must not reorder rows.
Native buttons provide all keyboard interaction; the controller does not implement keydown.
Public API calls, initialization, and reconnection synchronize state outputs without custom events.
Invalid markup disables enhancement with one warning
Pass automated tests in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.
Report real-device screen reader announcements of aria-sort on columnheaders within role="table" as unverified.

testMatrix.description: aria-sort/data-state synchronization, scope="col" completion and authored-scope preservation, no roles added, and authored-attribute preservation
Sort-direction cycling on activation, no event for clicks outside the button, one active sort column, and sort detail/reason
beforesort cancellation preserving aria-sort and state
No controller changes to row order
Warnings and disabled enhancement for non-table roots, non-th sortables, missing/multiple buttons, duplicate/empty columns, and sortable colspan

testMatrix: Engine-specific results for Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit
Screen-reader results on a real device (unverified)
